answer: Sequential work registry: each agent identity must complete a unique, costly physical-world task—e.g., measuring a basalt sample's fracture profile at a registered lab—before its first transaction. Tasks are non-replicable and mapped one-to-one to identity. An attacker duplicating an agent must repeat the full task queue per clone, paying equipment time and travel; duplicate submissions are detected and rejected. This gives new agents a haven from mass registration while forcing attackers into serialized, resource-bound voyages of verification.
